summary: Sets out the requirements for Operations, Administration, and Maintenance (OAM) needed to keep a Deterministic Networking network running as intended. DetNet (RFC 8655) aims to give bounded end-to-end latency across bridged and routed segments. This framework is meant to guide later work on specific OAM mechanisms.

eli5.summary: A train line promising on-time arrivals needs staff checking tracks and signals. This lists what checking and repair tools a network needs to keep delivery times reliable.

subtitle: Requirements for monitoring and maintaining deterministic networks

tldr.problem: Deterministic Networking aims to deliver packets with guaranteed low latency and loss, but managing such networks requires specialized operations and monitoring tools to track whether Service Level Objectives are being met.
tldr.mechanism: This framework specifies OAM (Operations, Administration, and Maintenance) requirements for DetNet systems, covering fault detection, performance measurement, and the coordination needed across forwarding and service sub-layers.
tldr.outcome: The framework guides future development of OAM protocols and tools tailored to DetNet's specific needs, enabling operators to maintain real-time visibility into network health.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Deterministic Networking (DetNet, defined in RFC 8655) aims to deliver packets with bounded latency, minimal loss, and correct ordering across both bridged and routed network segments. This creates strict performance contracts called Service Level Objectives (SLOs) for each flow. Unlike best-effort networks, DetNet must guarantee these SLOs even during congestion.

Operations, Administration, and Maintenance (OAM) tools are critical to keep such networks working. DetNet OAM must provide fault detection, localization, and real-time performance measurement without interfering with the data traffic it monitors. This document lists the functional requirements for DetNet OAM to help guide development of protocols and tools that meet these demands.
sections.eli5: DetNet promises speed and reliability, so teams need tools to check constantly that the network is behaving as promised, and to fix things fast when it does not.

sections.title: DetNet Architecture and OAM Layers
sections.content:
DetNet operates in two sub-layers: the forwarding sub-layer, which allocates resources and delivers packets through the underlay network, and the service sub-layer, which provides features like packet replication for redundancy and elimination of duplicates. OAM mechanisms exist for the forwarding sub-layer, but the service sub-layer requires new OAM procedures.

OAM works through Maintenance End Points (MEPs) at domain edges and Maintenance Intermediate Points (MIPs) along the path. DetNet uses both in-band OAM (test packets follow the same path and receive the same treatment as data) and out-of-band OAM (test traffic may follow different paths). Hybrid methods combine both approaches; for example, the Alternate-Marking Method marks data packets to measure delay and loss while avoiding separate test traffic.
sections.eli5: The network has two layers: one that forwards packets and one that protects them. Each needs different checks. Some checks ride along with real traffic, others use separate test messages.

sections.title: Operational OAM Functions
sections.content:
DetNet OAM must provide five core operational functions. Continuity Check detects whether a path still works one-way. Connectivity Verification adds a check for misconnection, detecting when traffic is arriving on the wrong path. Route Tracing maps which switches are in the path and discovers PREOF (Packet Replication, Elimination, Ordering Functions) locations. Fault Detection triggers alarms when performance degrades or faults occur, based on proactive monitoring or on-demand testing.

Fault Localization and Characterization narrow down where a failure is and what caused it, for example by correlating reports from multiple monitoring sessions or tracing the path of a failed flow. All test packets must follow the same path as the monitored data and share its Quality of Service treatment, so testing never introduces false congestion that would hide real problems.
sections.eli5: DetNet checks are like health tests: checking the heart is beating, checking the path is clear, mapping which doctors see the patient, spotting when something is wrong, then figuring out exactly what and where it broke.

sections.title: Performance Metrics and Resource Monitoring
sections.content:
DetNet administrators need real-time metrics to make decisions. Key metrics include queuing delay (how long packets wait at each switch), buffer occupancy per flow, and end-to-end performance measurements. Metrics must be collected per DetNet flow, per path, and per device so that operators can spot which path or device is misbehaving.

Because DetNet guarantees bounded latency and loss, average metrics are not enough: administrators must understand worst-case metrics, such as the maximum delay ever seen and the peak loss rate. The controller that places DetNet flows needs this timing information to predict whether new flows will violate existing SLOs, and to reconfigure the network if trends suggest failure is imminent.
sections.eli5: Operators need to know how long packets wait and how full the queues get, and they need the worst-case numbers, not just the average, so they can promise accurate delivery times.

sections.title: Maintaining Service Through Failures and Optimization
sections.content:
When DetNet provides redundancy through Packet Replication and Elimination, OAM must monitor and verify the replication and elimination functions to ensure they work correctly. If a flow is sent over multiple paths to survive link failures, OAM must detect when one path degrades and help the control plane decide whether to reroute.

The control plane continuously evaluates whether reconfiguration is needed, balancing two costs: the cost of suboptimal routing if resources are not used well, and the cost of reconfiguring the network (which temporarily reserves resources twice and sends control messages). OAM provides the real-time data needed to make these decisions and to maintain SLOs when network conditions change.
sections.eli5: When a flow travels two paths for safety, the network checks both paths are working. The controller looks at what OAM reports and decides whether to move traffic around to save resources or avoid bottlenecks.

sections.title: Key OAM Requirements for DetNet
sections.content:
The framework specifies that DetNet OAM MUST support both proactive monitoring (continuously checking every flow) and on-demand OAM (testing when the operator chooses). OAM MUST measure throughput, packet loss, out-of-order packets, delay, and delay variation. Test packets for unidirectional flows MUST be in-band, and for bidirectional flows, test packets MUST be in-band in both directions.

For the forwarding sub-layer, OAM MUST discover the maximum packet size (PMTU) and monitor resource levels (buffer utilization and transmission schedules). For the service sub-layer, OAM MUST discover relay nodes, find PREOF locations, collect configuration data from relay nodes, and support Alarm Indication Signaling. The framework recognizes that RIFT and MPLS environments need different implementations, so OAM must work with both DetNet data planes.
sections.eli5: The framework lists nine requirements: the system must check paths constantly, measure multiple kinds of slowness, ensure test packets behave like real traffic, and work with both Layer 2 and Layer 3 protection methods.
